notes: Variant treated as a front-to-chest seated overhead cable pulldown with thigh pad support, not a behind-the-neck pulldown. Grip is intentionally generic because the movement id does not specify wide, narrow, neutral, or supinated grip; direct evidence shows grip and forearm orientation can change activation, but recent multi-grip evidence still supports latissimus dorsi as the primary target. Rotator cuff support is marked as an anatomical inference from direct infraspinatus EMG rather than direct measurement of every cuff muscle. Local meshes now exist for all visible muscles: BodyParts3D covers teres major, biceps brachii, posterior deltoid, pectoralis major, rotator cuff, and middle/lower trapezius; Z-Anatomy MuscularSystem100.fbx supplies left and right latissimus dorsi because BodyParts3D 4.0 English ISA/PART-OF tables did not expose a latissimus dorsi muscle mesh. EMG evidence is acute and should not be read as direct hypertrophy or injury-risk evidence. Future work could split wide-pronated, narrow-neutral, reverse-grip, and behind-neck pulldowns into separate variants if the app needs grip-specific targeting.
